model.label: NM model (linear)
model.fit: Both clients scale linearly with state bytes (R² 0.99): NM at ~100 GB/h marginal, Geth ~2× slower at ~47 GB/h. The 5× NM→Geth point (57 h) is a loopback/single-peer-concurrency outlier — the properly-run 7× and 10× exactpivot cross-VM syncs land right on the linear trend.
model.predict7x: NM→NM 7× predicted ≈ 21 h (not yet run); measured NM→Geth 7× = 29 h 17 m.

finding: At 1× Geth is ~3.3× slower from a single NM peer. At 3.5× the trade-off flips two ways: NM finishes ~4 h sooner (it drains the storage-spam mega-tries as a clean final phase, while Geth front-loads them and stalls stop-go on each one), but Geth is far leaner on memory (~6.7 GB peak vs NM's ~18.4 GB). 5× NM → NM completes in ~17 h over the cross-VM link, ~1.6 TB on disk and ~26 GB RSS — same shape, the storage-spam mega-tries dominating the tail. At 10× the headline run, NM → NM, finishes in 27 h 24 m (3.16 TB on disk, ~35 GB peak RSS, single frozen peer at ~115 GB/h) — and the tail is now extreme: the final single storage trie alone took ~9 h, roughly a third of the whole sync, the x10 amplification of the ~3.31 M storage-spam clones that share one giant trie. NM → Geth is now measured all the way up too: 7× in 29 h 17 m and the headline 10× in 46 h 25 m — each producing a bootable Geth snapshot whose state root matches the canonical milestone root byte-for-byte (Geth commits the head, so this is confirmed directly via eth_getBlockByNumber, not only by heal-convergence). Both clients sit on a clean linear trend once the 5× loopback point is set aside — Geth simply runs at about half NM's single-peer rate. Every run reconstructs the source state root bit-for-bit.
geth5x: 5× NM → Geth (loopback, single peer) completed bit-identical in ~57 h at a steady 2.38M slots/min across the 7.79B slots — bound by single-peer request concurrency, not hardware (the box sat ~80% idle; both clients <1 core). Stock Nethermind couldn't even serve the x5 chain over devp2p until nethermind#12059: 8-billion-gas blocks make 26–47 MB bodies that overflow the 16 MB devp2p limit and desync the RLPx framer; the fix added an accurate size estimator + a 15 MB outgoing-bodies cap (0 framing errors across the whole run). Geth is ~3.3× slower than the NM target from a single peer — its per-peer in-flight request cap is the ceiling.
caveat: Wall time and bandwidth are single-dedicated-peer, controlled figures — read as relative scaling across state sizes, not real-world multi-peer sync time. Setups vary (the 5× NM→NM ran cross-VM, the 5× NM→Geth on loopback), so compare within a pair, not across. "n/s" = not sampled this run (final DB size + peak RSS weren't captured for 5× NM→Geth). Source states are frozen; NM uses the additive Sync.StaticSnapPivot flag (nethermind#11943), Geth --snap.exactpivot (go-ethereum#35265) + --snap.skipreceipts, plus --override.osaka/bpo and --Blocks.MaxGasLimit=9000000000 on the NM server to serve the 8-billion-gas x10 blocks. Still pending: 7× NM→NM, the Geth→NM mainnet-realism run, and the Besu / Reth / Erigon clients (issues #17 / #18 / #26).
